S or U: A2 [ S or U ] the area above the earth, in which clouds, the sun, etc. can be seen
› the sky in a particular state or place
（某種天氣狀況下或某地的）天空

example: a blue/cloudy/dark sky
藍色／多雲／陰暗的天空
Can you see those birds high up in the sky?
你能看到高空的那些鳥嗎?
We looked up at/into the sky at the sound of the plane.
我們聽到飛機的聲音後抬頭仰望天空。
For weeks we had cloudless blue skies.
好幾個禮拜以來，我們這裡的天空都是晴朗無雲，一片湛藍。
We're off to the sunny skies of Florida.
我們要離開這裡去享受佛羅里達晴朗的天空了。

NONE: › a bright, light blue colour
天藍色（的）
› an official person dressed in ordinary clothes, who carries a gun on an aircraft and whose job is to protect other passengers
空中便衣警察
› Sky-high prices or charges are very high.
（價格或收費）極高的（地），高昂的（地）

example: The price of oil went sky-high when war broke out.
戰爭爆發後，油價急遽上漲。

NONE: › a person who carries passengers' bags at an airport or receives them for putting onto an aircraft
機場行李搬運工
› a sport in which a person jumps from an aircraft and falls for as long as possible before opening a parachute
（延緩張傘的）跳傘運動
› to take control of a flying aircraft by force, usually in order to make political demands
（通常因為政治訴求而）劫機

example: See also
hijack verb

NONE: › a
lark noun(BIRD)
› a window built into a roof to allow light in
天窗

example: Putting in a skylight made the attic seem big and bright.
安裝天窗後，閣樓顯得又大又明亮。

NONE: › a shape or pattern made against the sky, especially by buildings
（尤指建築物在天空映襯下的）空中輪廓

example: You get a good view of the New York skyline from the Statue of Liberty.
從自由女神像上可以清楚地看到紐約的空中輪廓。

NONE: › to rise extremely quickly or make extremely quick progress towards success
暴漲，飛漲

example: Housing prices have skyrocketed in recent months.
近幾個月房價飛漲。
Synonym
rocket

NONE: › a very tall modern building, usually in a city
摩天大樓
› in the direction of the sky
向著天空地

example: He raised his eyes slowly skyward.
他慢慢抬頭向空中望去。
figurative At the news, share prices shot skyward (= suddenly increased a lot).
消息一傳出，股票價格一路暴漲。
